narrative.summary: In step 1, the task was set to classification on the status column. Step 2 selected PR-AUC as the primary metric for imbalanced data. Step 7 applied three approved cleaning actions before splitting, and step 8 held out 2,000 rows for the final test. Step 9 and step 10 issued statistical guidance and memory advice based on data skew and weak signals. Step 11 generated seven candidates, leading to step 16 where the supervisor chose the gradient boosting pipeline due to validity checks over an overfitted runner-up. Finally, step 17 kept the default tuned pipeline, and step 18 reported a final test PR-AUC score of 0.258 on the held-out set.

items.text: First we worked out what kind of problem this is: classification (target: status).
We fixed how success is measured before trying any model: pr_auc.
We cleaned the data using only fixes that cannot leak information: 3 approved actions applied.
We locked away part of the data to test the final model fairly: hold out 2000 rows until the winner is chosen.

We checked the statistics behind the data: Heavy skew in total_cents: add a power transform for linear and distance-based models.; Every single-feature effect is small: expect modest gains over the baseline and treat any large improvement with suspicion..
We looked for similar datasets we had seen before: 1 suggestion(s) passed to the Architect and Critic as advice.
We tried several kinds of model: 7 candidates; all go to the Critic (no automatic selection).
The agents debated which model to use: c4_gradient_boosting_r1.
We fine-tuned the best options: c4_gradient_boosting_r1.
Finally we tested the chosen model once on the locked-away data: pr_auc 0.2580 on 2000 held-out rows.

narrative_beginner.summary: In step 1, the system set the goal to classification using a column named status. Step 2 chose a matching scoring method because the data was unevenly distributed. Steps 7 and 8 cleaned the data and saved 2000 rows to test the final model safely. Steps 9, 10, and 11 provided data advice, checked for skewness, and generated potential models. Finally, steps 16, 17, and 18 selected a gradient boosting model because it avoided overfitting, scoring 0.258 on the hidden test rows.

business.headline: The model is no better than a simple baseline beyond chance. The score is 0.258, compared to the baseline of 0.25, giving a relative lift of 3.2%. This small gain of about 0.008 is well within what chance produces on 2,000 held-out rows, with a 95% confidence interval ranging from -0.002 to 0.021.

research.note: Context, not a literature review. Closest notes: The Precision-Recall Plot Is More Informative than the ROC Plot When Evaluating Binary Classifiers on Imbalanced Datasets (Saito and Rehmsmeier, 2015): On imbalanced data, precision-recall curves reveal weaknesses that ROC curves hide.; A New Family of Power Transformations to Improve Normality or Symmetry (Yeo and Johnson, 2000): A power transform that, unlike Box-Cox, works for zero and negative values.; The Relationship Between Precision-Recall and ROC Curves (Davis and Goadrich, 2006): Proves a curve dominates in ROC space if and only if it dominates in PR space, and discusses PR interpolation.
